chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who set out in

the months of Hajj performing Umrah, then returned to his country. He said: There is no harm, and if he performs Hajj in his year and performs Hajj alone, there is no blood-offering (dam) upon him. Indeed, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) set out before Tarwiyah to Iraq, and he had entered Mecca performing Umrah.

key_terms.أَشْهُرُ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi'dah, and first 10 days of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who performs Umrah in the Hajj months and returns home before performing Hajj?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Isfahaniyyah highlights the permissibility of 'Umrat al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) even when performed in separate years, a view supported by the precedent of Imam al-Husayn (AS) who entered Mecca for Umrah before his journey to Kufa. Shaykh al-Tusi includes this in the chapter on 'Umrah al-Mubtulah' to clarify that the absence of a blood-offering (dam) applies when the pilgrim returns to their homeland, distinguishing it from cases where one remains in the Haram boundaries. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of ritual acts based on Prophetic and Imami practice rather than strict chronological simultaneity.
